Find the area $A$ of the region in the $xy$-plane that is bounded by the curve $y={x}^{2}-{sin}^{2}⁡(x),$ the $x$-axis, and the lines $x=\frac{\pi }{2}$ and $x=\pi ,$ as shown above. Do not round the answer.

$A=$
{{field-1}}
feedback.worked_solution:
The area of the region bounded by the curve $y={x}^{2}-{sin}^{2}⁡x,$ the $x$-axis and the lines $x=\frac{\pi }{2}$ and $x=\pi $ is

$$
A={\int }_{\pi /2}^{\pi }({x}^{2}-{sin}^{2}⁡x)\,\text{d}x.
$$

Let's recall the double-angle formula for cosine that involves the ${sin}^{2}$ term: 

$$
\operatorname{cos}⁡2x=1-2{sin}^{2}⁡x
$$

We can rearrange the above formula as

$$
\frac{1}{2}(\operatorname{cos}⁡2x-1)=-{sin}^{2}⁡x.
$$

Hence, the area of the region is

$$
\begin{aligned}A & ={\int }_{\pi /2}^{\pi }({x}^{2}-{sin}^{2}⁡x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{\pi /2}^{\pi }({x}^{2}+\frac{1}{2}(\operatorname{cos}⁡2x-1))\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{\pi /2}^{\pi }({x}^{2}+\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡2x-\frac{1}{2})\,\text{d}x \\  & ={(\frac{{x}^{3}}{3}+\frac{1}{4}\operatorname{sin}⁡2x-\frac{1}{2}x)|}_{\pi /2}^{\pi } \\  & =(\frac{{\pi }^{3}}{3}+\frac{1}{4}\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\pi )-\frac{\pi }{2})-(\frac{(\pi /2)^{3}}{3}+\frac{1}{4}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi )-\frac{1}{2}\cdot \frac{\pi }{2}) \\  & =(\frac{{\pi }^{3}}{3}-\frac{\pi }{2})-(\frac{{\pi }^{3}}{24}-\frac{\pi }{4}) \\  & =\frac{7{\pi }^{3}}{24}-\frac{\pi }{4}.\end{aligned}
$$
